page: Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-300s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, supporting multithreading with 2 threads per core. System memory is configured at 16.0 GB RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB allocation per vCPU. Local storage is bundled as a 300 GB NVMe SSD. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and contains no dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded performance. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 3213.28, placing it in the top ten percent, and a Geekbench single-core score of 2122.0, placing in the top twenty-five percent. Multithreaded metrics remain in the middle tier, with stress-ng multi-core testing scoring 25653.07 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 10810.0. Large-block memory bandwidth measures 118.62 GB/sec for uncached reads and 68.98 GB/sec for writes. Performance on small 135M parameter language models reaches 240.07 generation tokens per second, but prompt processing for medium 7B models falls into the bottom quartile at 25.18 tokens per second.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio yields high compute density at a balanced cost profile, favoring execution threads over large memory capacity. The integrated 300 GB NVMe SSD delivers reliable I/O performance, supporting static web serving throughput of 9.2 GB/sec and Redis operations at 16.48 million operations per second. However, memory-intensive database architectures and large model inference workloads are limited by the 16.0 GB RAM capacity. This instance is best suited for CI/CD compilation, text processing pipelines, batch compute tasks, and microservice backends.
description: Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-300s-amd belongs to the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs from a 4-core AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, 16.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD. Operating at a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation without hardware accelerators, the system emphasizes compute density and single-threaded performance. Benchmark measurements confirm strong single-core efficiency, placing in the top 10% in stress-ng single-core tests and top 25% in Geekbench single-core tests, alongside average multi-core metrics. Memory throughput reaches 118.62 GB/sec for large block reads, while static web serving achieves 9.2 GB/sec. Due to the modest RAM allocation relative to its 8 dedicated vCPUs, the instance exhibits lower performance in large language model processing but maintains reliable execution for code compilation, continuous integration pipelines, batch text processing, and compute-focused web applications requiring fast local NVMe storage.
